sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and learned counsel for the State and learned counsel for the Informant.

2. The Petitioner is an accused in G.R. Case No.155 of 2022 pending on the file of learned ADJ-Cum-P.O., Special Court, POCSO, Sundargarh, arising out of Kutra P.S. Case No.144 of 2022 for commission of the offence under Sections 363/366/376(2)(n)/376(D) of IPC and read with Sec-6 of the POCSO Act.

3. Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s. 439 Cr.P.C by the learned A.D.J.,-cum-PO Special Court, under POCSO Act, Sundargarh, by order dated 04.04.2023 in the aforementioned case, the present BLAPL has been filed.
4. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the Petitioner is in custody since 22.08.2022 and charge sheet has been filed on 30.09.2022, under Section 376(D) of IPC against the present Petitioner.
5. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the present accused person has not been identified in T.I. Parade, hence he may be released on bail.
6. Learned counsel for the State on the other hand submits that import of such T.I Parade has to be Dillip Kullu vs State Of Odisha ....

7. An affidavit has been filed on the behalf of the informant, mother of the victim indicating that the matter has been compromised and victim girl and the informant have no objections, if the Petitioner is released on bail.
8. Keeping in view the provisions of POCSO Act, this Court is not inclined to take into account the affidavit filed by the informant.
9. Perused the 164 Cr.P.C. statement of the victim and keeping in view the nature of allegation against the present Petitioner, this Court is not inclined to entertain this bail application.
10. Leave is granted to renew his prayer after examination of the victim.

11. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
(V. NARASINGH) Judge Soumya Signed by: SOUMYA RANJAN SAMAL Location: High Court of Orissa Date: 22-Jul-2023 15:28:50 Dillip Kullu vs State Of Odisha ....
